scenarios: Load creates an invisible placeholder, never a colour copy
Runtime uses an isolated native shader at queue998
The original source mesh and material are not mutated
Every source triangle has both depth windings
Complete nested source transforms are baked relative to the IVA
Mask construction adds no physical collider
Native OnLoad material replacement is repaired without mutating its singleton
Missing or stale native mask reference is rebound
An unrelated configured mask is not hijacked
Start before OnLoad and native cache readiness is harmless
Late runtime instance rediscovers serialized marker with cleared private fields
Repeated OnLoad retains exactly one complete mask
Camera transitions match native modes and preserve external mask
Creation after Flight camera event still sets correct visibility
Null camera manager does not break loading or material initialization
Missing shader never renders original colour and recovers when ready
Unavailable asset loader is retried instead of aborting IVA compilation
Unsupported shader disables only the added renderer
Late colour-material replacement is repaired before rendering
Late queue, shader, layer and renderer changes are repaired locally
Stable frame updates allocate no additional materials
Two IVA instances own different materials and state
Destruction releases only the helper's owned material
Missing source reports a bounded error and leaves original glass
Invalid mesh indices are rejected before creating a mask
Empty source is rejected before creating a mask
Non-finite source geometry is rejected before creating a mask
Conflicting generated-name object is left untouched
Missing INTERNAL context reports instead of throwing
Loading scene does not create runtime materials or touch native camera state
scope_limitations: Executes exact production helper with dependency doubles; does not execute KSP/Unity, GPU shaders, real camera compositing, prefab serialization, native FreeIVA OnLoad, or ModuleManager.
Geometry source checks and actual API compilation are separate.
Render-queue hazard and recovery scenarios establish code behavior, not the cause of an unrecorded user GPU frame.
